670	// Compact reclaims history: values that were overwritten or deleted and are
671	// not needed by any open snapshot or cursor are dropped from memory and the
672	// write-ahead log is atomically rewritten, so the directory occupies less
673	// space than before whenever reclaimable history existed.
674	//
675	// When a checkpoint chain is live, compaction keeps the generations inside
676	// the retention window and re-anchors them against the replacement log: that
677	// log is written as one segment per surviving layer (its prefix reproducing
678	// the layer's terminal state at a fresh cut), followed by the post-window
679	// changes and the snapshot-count meta, and the rebuilt layers reference those
680	// cuts. Generations outside the window are retired together with the old
681	// chain and stop occupying space immediately.
682	//
683	// Every open snapshot keeps its exact fixed view; every open cursor keeps
684	// paging through its exact fixed sequence, and the one version per key its
685	// view shows stays in the rewritten log until the cursor closes; the next
686	// compaction then reclaims it and shrinks the directory further. A process
687	// killed at any point during compaction reopens in a complete commit state,
688	// with every successful write, deletion and the cumulative snapshot count
689	// intact; no intermediate file needs a second compaction or checkpoint to
690	// repair.
691	//
692	// Compact serializes with writes, deletes, snapshots, cursor opens, closing
693	// and other compactions (the group-commit leader and every other mutator
694	// take the same lock); concurrent or repeated calls queue and all return nil.
695	// Compacting a closed store returns an error wrapping fs.ErrClosed.
696	func (s *Store) Compact() error {
697		s.mu.Lock()
698		defer s.mu.Unlock()
699		if s.closed.Load() {
700			return errStoreClosed
701		}
702	
703		cur := s.current.Load()
704	
705		// Pinned versions, keyed by commit sequence (globally unique). The
706		// current head of every live key in the latest view is retained; each
707		// open cursor additionally pins the single head version its fixed view
708		// shows for every present key in its range. A deleted key's tombstone is
709		// retained only when a cursor still reads an older value under it, so
710		// replay links that value as the tombstone's predecessor; otherwise the
711		// key is dropped from the rewritten log altogether, as before.
712		pinned := make(map[uint64]*node)
713		keySeqs := make(map[string][]uint64)
714		cursorPins := make(map[string]bool)
715		pin := func(k string, n *node) {
716			if n == nil {
717				return
718			}
719			if _, ok := pinned[n.seq]; !ok {
720				pinned[n.seq] = n
721				keySeqs[k] = append(keySeqs[k], n.seq)
722			}
723		}
724		for _, c := range s.openCursors() {
725			for _, k := range c.keys {
726				cursorPins[k] = true
727				pin(k, c.v.lookup(k)) // exactly the version this cursor pages out
728			}
729		}
730		for k, n := range keySetOf(cur) {
731			if n.present || cursorPins[k] {
732				pin(k, n) // live head, or a tombstone shielding a pinned value
733			}
734		}
735	
736		plan := buildCompactionPlan(pinned, keySeqs)
737		snapshotCount := s.snapshots.Load()
738	
739		// The surviving window, oldest first. Layers before it are retired.
740		window := checkpointWindow
741		if window > len(s.chain) {
742			window = len(s.chain)
743		}
744		first := len(s.chain) - window
745		windowLayers := s.chain[first:]
746		hadChain := len(s.chain) > 0
747		// paired reports any checkpoint — layered chain or a legacy single file —
748		// whose cut belongs to the WAL about to be replaced. It must be withdrawn
749		// before the swap so no checkpoint is ever read against a different log.
750		paired := hadChain || s.legacyLive
751	
752		// Phase 1 (nothing live is touched yet): build and sync the complete
753		// replacement log, and when layers survive, the matching staged chain.
754		// Any failure here removes the staged files and leaves the store and the
755		// old WAL/chain exactly as they were, so committing can continue.
756		var seg *segmentedWAL
757		if !hadChain {
758			if err := buildCompactWAL(s.dir, plan.histories(), snapshotCount); err != nil {
759				return err
760			}
761		} else {
762			// Full terminal state at each window layer's watermark, composed from
763			// the complete old chain (including the generations about to retire).
764			termStates := make([][]checkpointEntry, window)
765			for w := 0; w < window; w++ {
766				termStates[w] = composeLayers(s.chain[:first+w+1])
767			}
768			seg = planSegmentedWAL(plan, windowLayers, termStates, cur)
769			if err := buildSegmentedCompactArtifacts(s.dir, seg, snapshotCount); err != nil {
770				return err
771			}
772		}
773	
774		// Phase 2: the replacement must never meet a paired checkpoint on reopen.
775		// Durably withdraw the whole layered chain and/or the legacy file while
776		// the old wal.log is still in place; a crash after this but before the
777		// rename simply replays the old log in full. Failure precedes any
778		// stateful move, so drop the staged files and leave the store untouched.
779		if paired {
780			if err := retireChain(s.dir); err != nil {
781				removeStaleCompact(s.dir)
782				removeStagedChain(s.dir)
783				return err
784			}
785			s.legacyLive = false
786		}
787		oldWAL := s.wal
788		if err := oldWAL.close(); err != nil {
789			// Staged files have not become state of record; remove them and
790			// reopen a writer on the untouched old log, so no repair-only
791			// intermediate lingers and the next commit proceeds.
792			removeStaleCompact(s.dir)
793			removeStagedChain(s.dir)
794			reopened, openErr := openWALWriter(s.dir, -1)
795			if openErr != nil {
796				return err
797			}
798			s.wal = reopened
799			return err
800		}
801		// Phase 3: atomically rename the temp over wal.log, force the directory
802		// and open a writer on the new log. If the rename never landed the old
803		// log is intact and committing continues (staged chain is dropped).
804		nextWAL, renamed, installErr := installCompactWAL(s.dir)
805		if nextWAL == nil {
806			// The rename landed but the new log cannot be opened: the directory
807			// is not in a state where further commits are safe, so mark the
808			// store closed rather than leaving a handle only another compaction
809			// could repair.
810			s.closed.Store(true)
811			s.wal = nil
812			return installErr
813		}
814		s.wal = nextWAL
815		if renamed {
816			s.current.Store(plan.freshView())
817			if hadChain {
818				// dropCheckpoint clears any in-memory and on-disk chain so the
819				// next Checkpoint starts a fresh base with no O_EXCL collision.
820				dropCheckpoint := func() {
821					s.chain = nil
822					s.dirty = nil
823					os.RemoveAll(checkpointDirPath(s.dir))
824				}
825				if window == 0 {
826					dropCheckpoint()
827					removeStagedChain(s.dir)
828				} else if err := activateStagedChain(s.dir); err != nil {
829					// The new WAL is already live; rather than leave a half
830					// installed chain, run with no live checkpoint. The next
831					// Checkpoint establishes a fresh base.
832					dropCheckpoint()
833				} else {
834					info, ierr := readChain(s.dir)
835					if ierr != nil || len(info.layers) != window {
836						dropCheckpoint()
837					} else {
838						s.chain = info.layers
839						s.dirty = seg.tailKeys
840					}
841				}
842			}
843		} else if hadChain {
844			// Rename failed; the old WAL stayed. retireChain already removed the
845			// old chain, so drop the staged replacement as well: no checkpoint
846			// pairs with this WAL. Committing continues; the next Checkpoint heals.
847			removeStagedChain(s.dir)
848			s.chain = nil
849			s.dirty = nil
850		}
851		return installErr
852	}

854	// keySetOf returns the distinct keys present anywhere in the view.
855	func keySetOf(v *view) map[string]*node {
856		out := make(map[string]*node)
857		v.rangeEach(func(k string, n *node) bool {
858			out[k] = n
859			return true
860		})
861		return out
862	}

864	// Checkpoint appends one self-describing, checksummed layer to the checkpoint
865	// chain so the next Open seeds memory from the longest intact layer prefix
866	// and replays only the write-ahead log written after it, instead of replaying
867	// the whole log. The first layer (the base) holds complete committed state;
868	// every later layer covers only commits after the layer it builds on.
869	// Checkpoint changes nothing visible: every committed write and deletion, the
870	// cumulative snapshot count and every open snapshot or cursor are unaffected,
871	// and reads keep hitting memory without touching disk.
872	//
873	// Producing a layer and making it live are two distinct steps: the layer is
874	// captured under the write lock, built fully under a temporary name and
875	// forced to stable storage, then atomically renamed into place and linked to
876	// the previous layer by a content hash. A kill at any instant leaves either
877	// the old complete chain or the chain extended by one complete layer; reopen
878	// observes one complete committed state, never a half layer (staging debris
879	// is swept on the next open).
880	//
881	// Only checkpointWindow newest generations are kept: appending past the
882	// window rebuilds the chain with the oldest surviving layer as a fresh full
883	// base against the unchanged WAL and deletes the retired layers immediately.
884	//
885	// Checkpoint serializes with writes, batch commits, snapshots, cursor opens,
886	// compaction and closing (it takes the same write lock), but never with
887	// lock-free reads: Get, scans, snapshot reads and cursor paging proceed while
888	// it runs. A batch stays wholly on one side of the captured cut, and history
889	// pinned by open snapshots or cursors is left untouched. On a closed store
890	// Checkpoint returns an error wrapping fs.ErrClosed.
891	func (s *Store) Checkpoint() error {
892		s.mu.Lock()
893		defer s.mu.Unlock()
894		if s.closed.Load() {
895			return errStoreClosed
896		}
897	
898		offset, err := s.wal.position()

900			return err
901		}
902		cur := s.current.Load()
903		snaps := s.snapshots.Load()
904

906			// First layer: full base state. This also upgrades a legacy
907			// single-file directory: the old file is removed once the base is
908			// staged, and the WAL it pairs with has not changed.
909			layer := capturedLayer{
910				index:   0,
911				entries: captureView(cur),
912				offset:  uint64(offset),
913				seq:     s.nextSeq,
914				snaps:   snaps,
915			}
916			if err := installLayer(s.dir, layer); err != nil {
917				return err
918			}
919			if err := removeLegacyCheckpoint(s.dir); err != nil {
920				return err
921			}
922			s.legacyLive = false
923		} else {
924			last := s.chain[len(s.chain)-1]
925			layer := capturedLayer{
926				index:   last.index + 1,
927				prevCRC: last.crc,
928				entries: captureDelta(cur, s.dirty),
929				offset:  uint64(offset),
930				seq:     s.nextSeq,
931				snaps:   snaps,

937

940			return err
941		}
942		s.chain = info.layers

944

946		// layers, rebuilt as a standalone chain against the same unchanged WAL.
947		if len(s.chain) > checkpointWindow {

949				return err
950			}
951		}
952		return nil
953	}
954	
955	// rebaseChainToWindow rebuilds the live chain so only the newest
956	// checkpointWindow layers remain: the oldest kept layer becomes a fresh full
957	// base (materialized from the complete in-memory chain) at its existing WAL
958	// cut, and the layers after it keep their delta content at their existing
959	// cuts. The WAL is not touched.
960	func (s *Store) rebaseChainToWindow() error {
961		keep := checkpointWindow
962		if keep > len(s.chain) {
963			keep = len(s.chain)
964		}
965		first := len(s.chain) - keep
966		// Materialize full terminal state at the oldest kept layer.
967		full := composeLayers(s.chain[:first+1])
968		newLayers := make([]capturedLayer, 0, keep)
969		newLayers = append(newLayers, capturedLayer{
970			index: 0, entries: full,
971			offset: uint64(s.chain[first].offset),
972			seq:    s.chain[first].seq,
973			snaps:  s.chain[first].snaps,
974		})
975		for j := first + 1; j < len(s.chain); j++ {
976			newLayers = append(newLayers, capturedLayer{
977				index:   uint32(j - first),
978				entries: s.chain[j].entries,
979				offset:  uint64(s.chain[j].offset),

982			})
983		}

997	func composeLayers(layers []layerState) []checkpointEntry {
998		term := make(map[string]checkpointEntry)
999		for _, l := range layers {

1001				term[e.key] = e // later layer wins; tombstones survive as tombstones
1002			}
1003		}
1004		out := make([]checkpointEntry, 0, len(term))
1005		for _, e := range term {

1007		}

1013	// bounds are immutable after opening, so reading their fields here needs no

1020			cs = append(cs, c)

1023	}

1025	// Snapshot acquires a stable view. It never observes writes committed after
1026	// it returns, and keeps serving that view regardless of later writes,
1027	// deletes or Store.Close, until the Snapshot itself is closed.
1028	func (s *Store) Snapshot() (*Snapshot, error) {
1029		s.mu.Lock()
1030		defer s.mu.Unlock()
1031		if s.closed.Load() {
1032			return nil, errStoreClosed
1033		}
1034		count := s.snapshots.Add(1)
1035		if err := s.wal.appendMeta(count); err != nil {
1036			s.snapshots.Add(^uint64(0))
1037			return nil, err
1038		}
1039		snap := &Snapshot{store: s}
1040		snap.v.Store(s.current.Load())
1041		return snap, nil
1042	}
1043	
1044	// Get reads key from the snapshot's fixed view. Old values overwritten or
1045	// deleted afterwards are still readable; keys created afterwards, empty
1046	// keys and keys absent or deleted when the snapshot was taken are misses. A
1047	// read from a closed snapshot is also a plain miss, never an error. The
1048	// returned bytes are owned by the caller.
1049	func (s *Snapshot) Get(key string) ([]byte, bool) {

1052		}

1069	}

1078			s.mu.Unlock()

1080		}

1082		s.wal = nil
1083		s.mu.Unlock()
1084	
1085		return wal.close()
1086	}

A ring count below one or beyond the chain's ring count, a chain directory
that is missing, not a directory, missing its head, or itself damaged (a
missing ring, a broken link, a non-continuous watermark, truncation, a
checksum failure or an unknown version), or a chain advanced concurrently
during the merge, rejects the whole operation with an error satisfying
`errors.Is(err, fs.ErrInvalid)` and leaves the chain exactly as it was.
`MergeChain` on a closed store returns an error satisfying
`errors.Is(err, fs.ErrClosed)`.

### Online verification and self-healing

`VerifyBackupChain(chainDir)` checks a chain online, so corruption is found
without waiting for a restore. It streams the chain in chain order — the head
manifest, the head segments one at a time, then the dense rings one at a time
— and checks each link in it: the head artifact, the dense 1-based ring
order, every ring's predecessor content-CRC link, head/ring watermark
continuity, the per-segment and whole-file checksums and the format version.
It reads in bounded segments and never loads the whole chain or the whole
keyspace into memory. It takes no store lock: writes, batch commits, snapshot
open/close, cursor paging, checkpoints, compactions, incremental exports and
lock-free reads proceed while it runs and reads keep hitting memory instead
of waiting on the verifier's disk reads.

A healthy chain verifies and is left byte-for-byte unchanged. When a ring (or a
suffix of rings) is damaged — missing, truncated, checksum-bad, of an unknown
version, unlinked, with a discontinuous watermark or a regressing snapshot
count — the chain is degraded at ring granularity to its longest intact
prefix. The damaged suffix is moved, unchanged, into a sibling
`<chain>.quarantine-*` directory that also carries a self-describing marker
naming every isolated file; the isolated artifacts are kept for diagnosis and
take no further part in restores, merges or incremental exports. The chain
directory then holds the head plus exactly the dense intact rings, validates
as one whole, and:

- restores byte-for-byte to the state and cumulative snapshot count at the
  last intact watermark, with batch atomicity and within-batch last-write-wins
  preserved and deletes covered by merged rings never resurrected;
- merges and accepts further `BackupIncremental` rings in the degraded ring
  order (the next ring continues the dense numbering and links at the degraded
  tip), and the appended rings still pass whole-chain verification.

Damage at the head has no intact prefix in front of it, so such a chain, like
a chain with a foreign entry or a missing/non-directory path, is rejected

**Online chain verification and self-healing** (`verify.go`, new):
- `(*Store).VerifyBackupChain(chainDir)` streams the chain in chain order — head manifest → head segments → dense rings one at a time — reusing the existing streaming readers (`streamHeadSegments`, `scanRing`), so it checks head artifact, dense ring order, predecessor content-CRC links, watermark continuity, per-segment/whole-file checksums and format version in bounded memory, never loading the whole chain or keyspace.
- Healthy chains are left byte-for-byte unchanged. A damaged ring suffix is **isolated at ring granularity**: the replacement chain (hard-linked intact prefix) is validated whole, then committed with the same two-rename swap a merge uses. A kill at any point leaves either the old chain or the complete new one; suffix extraction into a self-describing `<chain>.quarantine-*` sibling (with a `QUARANTINE.txt` naming every isolated file) happens only after the replacement is live.
- `sweepVerifyDebris` finishes/undoes an interrupted swap (rollback between renames, suffix quarantine after install, orphaned-staging cleanup) and runs on open (standing down behind a live lease) and at the start of every chain operation.
- Verification takes `backupMu` (never `mu`) and the chain lease, so it doesn't block commits, batch sync, snapshots, cursors, checkpoints, compaction or lock-free reads; lease contention fails whole with `fs.ErrInvalid`; closed store → `fs.ErrClosed`. No third error type.

**Post-degradation semantics**: Restore on the *degraded* chain reproduces the exact keys/values and cumulative snapshot count at the last intact watermark; merge/append continue the renumbered dense ring order with intact CRC links; isolated rings never rejoin restore/merge/export. Un-degraded damaged chains still reject wholesale from `Restore`/`MergeChain`/`BackupIncremental` (existing behavior and tests preserved) — self-healing is deliberately opt-in via the verify call.

**Synthetic-tombstone watermark fix** (`incremental.go`): a zero-span ring (`endWM == startWM`) is now legal when it holds only boundary tombstones for deletes compaction forgot while the tip didn't advance; both the writer-side guard and the `scanRing` reader accept exactly that shape and reject any put/other boundary entry. The delete still reads as a miss after synthesis.

**Docs/tests**: README gained an "Online verification and self-healing" section and the new API entry; `verify_test.go` covers every corruption kind (8 damage types), head-damage rejection, prefix correctness vs. saved stages, as-is quarantine bytes, append/merge continuation, batch-semantics preservation, lease contention, concurrent activity, the zero-span tombstone scenario, and crash-sweep/open recovery — plus the full existing suite remains green under `go vet`, `gofmt`, and `-race`.
